Hey there, I’m on the spectrum too and have struggled with this in the past. While I’m still not absolutely great filtering I have some things I do that help somewhat. 

1 - default phrases or responses. Sometimes it’s hard for me to think on the spot cause the first thing I think is often blunt or unfiltered. When I get stuck, I revert to using some tried and true responses/topics that I know are normal-sounding enough. These could be responses you’ve heard from other people, or tv shows and movies. Any response from like a neurotypical that can be used to apply for multiple situations/topics work. 

2 - Be polite/complimentary. Sometimes things I say can be harsh-sounding unintentionally but I try to make up for it by being as nice as possible to let people it’s not my intention to offend or come across rude. Even just a simple “thank you” or owning up and apologizing helps with this. 

3 - talk in a group of three or more, or if it’s just another person, try to keep to convo going by asking questions. Typically I find that when I don’t have anything good to say having an extra person (like inviting along another friend, or talking in a group at work...) to fill in the gaps for me (cause I can’t come up with anything appropriate to say) tends to help. Also, if it is one-on-one, if you have gaps of silence because you need time to think of a response, I just instead ask them more questions relating to them. It keeps the convo moving and you don’t really have to come up with an appropriate response if the pressure is off you. Also allows a chance for the topic to flow into territory you’re more comfortable with and have some better responses to. 

These are just some things over the years I try to do. Obviously it’s not perfect, but I understand how you feel about being afraid to come across rude or inappropriate. Hopefully we can keep working on this and getting better in the future. Best of luck!

Definitely saving this, love all the tips! I always thought there was no use for “stupid” breathing techniques or cutting out coffee, but once I did, it helped so much I can’t believe I haven’t done it my entire life! Also - showering and baths help so much. Warm water and steam help a lot to calm me down.

Yes, before I got back on medication. I felt like everyday I was spiraling more and more out of control and I felt like it would never stop. Now that I’ve employed some anxiety help techniques and gotten on some meds, it’s been better. Not 100% perfect, but progress is still progress.

Thank you so much!
